Competitor News.title: Visa Las Vegas!
Competitor News.summary: Visa Las Vegas! Oracle Red Bull Racing
bullets: Oracle Red Bull Racing will run a golden chrome championship livery on Alisha Palmowski's No.21 Academy Programme car, with Visa's signature colours inspiring an electric blue gradient. It debuts at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit on Thursday 19 November, the final round of the 2026 F1 Academy season.

Palmowski, who won the F1 Academy title at the United States Grand Prix, will also wear a matching special-edition race suit. Visa said the collaboration celebrates her title and supports emerging athletes, and the team said it gives her a fitting send-off from F1 Academy.
Competitor News.copy:
Following her F1 ACADEMY title victory at the United States Grand Prix, Alisha will take to the track in Sin City with a bespoke golden championship livery, celebrating her title-winning season in style. The special-edition livery will make its debut at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit on Thursday 19 November, marking the final round of the 2026 season.

Commemorating her status as F1 ACADEMY Champion, every partner logo on the Red Bull Racing Academy Programme car and her No.21 will feature a golden chrome finish, set against an electric blue gradient backdrop inspired by Visa's signature colours. The design will be enhanced by a light-reactive metallic finish, creating a striking look fit for a champion under the bright lights of Las Vegas.

Wider Sports News.title: PGA Tour calls LIV Golf subpoena a fishing expedition
Wider Sports News.summary: PGA Tour calls LIV Golf subpoena a fishing expedition The Straits Times
Wider Sports News.copy:

For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans. Wider Sports News.title: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season
Wider Sports News.summary: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season Sports Media Watch
Wider Sports News.copy:
The timeline is accelerating for the NFL’s expedited media rights negotiations. John Ourand of Puck reported Thursday that the NFL is now believed to want its new media rights deals completed before the new season begins in September, earlier than the fall timeframe that had been previously reported. The league is expected to negotiate and announce its new deals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, Ourand wrote, with all of them taking effect immediately.

Technically, the NFL does not have the ability to exit its current media rights deals until after the 2029 season at the earliest (2030 for ESPN), but there is little expectation that any of the league’s partners will oppose the expedited talks. According to Ourand, it is believed that the new contracts will run through the 2033 or 2034 seasons, meaning that the existing rightsholders can lock up NFL rights for the next seven or eight years by agreeing to the early talks. Currently, the networks are guaranteed only four additional seasons if they choose to wait for the league’s contractual opt-out.

The sports media rights marketplace is preparing for a shakeup. As the decade nears its end and the NFL almost certainly exits its current set of media rights deals, networks and streamers are preparing for what could be a monumental shift in the industry. Legacy broadcasters continue to consolidate or get spun off from their corporate parents, while streaming giants continue to battle each other for engagement. The NFL is the 3,000-pound gorilla in the room that will dictate how networks and streamers approach other media rights opportunities in the next several years.

Major properties that will be on the market before or during NFL negotiations include the 2030 FIFA World Cup (set to be awarded by the end of 2026), MLB, NHL, and Premier League (all of which expire in 2028), Big Ten and PGA Tour (2030), and NASCAR (2031).

On 16 November 2026 a Milan court placed the Italian branch of Revolut, the bank that gives its name to the Audi Revolut F1 Team, under judicial administration for one year. The bank stays open, though, and the order is not a conviction: that is why I believe Audi will leave the contract alone. The real risk lies in communications, because for a bank the product is trust.

Suppose you are the head of communications at a Formula 1 team. One morning the name written on your car is in the headlines for a reason that has nothing to do with overtaking. What do you do? Rugby.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
Rugby.summary: Former England captain Lewis Moody joins the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge.

Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks.

Rugby.title: England set for ANOTHER World Rugby fine after epic All Blacks haka response

Rugby.copy:
Steve Borthwick's side recreated their famous V-shaped formation from the 2019 Rugby World Cup, with England legend Lewis Moody leading the response. The 2003 World Cup winner stood at the front as Maro Itoje and his teammates spread across the pitch to face New Zealand's traditional challenge.

It was an emotional moment for Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) in September 2025. The former England captain was helping launch his new Front Up to MND campaign, which aims to raise money for research into the disease.

Rugby.title: Unbeaten World Rugby Nations Cup winners name teams for final bout
Rugby.summary: The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament's best.
Rugby.copy:
The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament’s best. The USA enjoyed a blowout win over Romania in round 5 to secure their Pool A crown after four tight wins to begin the inaugural competition, while Georgia’s supremacy in Pool B has never been challenged, and they’ve emerged with a competition-best points differential of +124 through five rounds of action.

There is no further silverware on offer for the teams, but there’s an air of serendipity in the matchup coming in the final round of the competition. USA head coach Scott Lawrence has made just one change to the starting XV that put 53 points on Romania last weekend, with Mitch Wilson replacing Perry Mayo at fullback. And Georgia’s Pierre-Henry Broncan has also opted for as much continuity as possible, only promoting loosehead prop Sergo Abramishvili and halfback Gela Aprasidzeto to the starting team.

Returning from Red Roses camp to prepare for a new Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR) season, Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt was hit by the realisation of how much had changed. For the first time in three campaigns, Gloucester-Hartpury enter not as defending champions but as challengers; Saracens, the league’s first dynastic power, were restored to their throne in June with a final demolition job against the upstart Trailfinders. A relinquishing of their crown precipitated a summer of drastic change – gone from an environment known colloquially known as “The Circus” are, among others, Zoe Stratford, Tatyana Heard, Sarah Beckett, Sisilia Tuipulotu, Bethan Lewis and Kelsey Jones.

Or, as ringmaster Hunt puts it: “Pretty much my friendship group has all gone.” New mother Stratford (nee Aldcroft) was her business partner and co-captain; having lost charismatic coach Sean Lynn to Wales last year, there is certainly a different feel about the place.

South Africa men’s 15s head coach Rassie Erasmus has been suspended for six international matches with immediate effect. The sanction follows a review of wide-ranging comments made by Erasmus at a media conference this week concerning officiating during the Springboks’ Nations Championship match against France last Friday.

An independent panel imposed the sanction under World Rugby’s Match Official Abuse Sanction Process. Introduced in July 2026 with national member unions, competitions, International Rugby Match Officials (IRMO) and International Rugby Players’ Association (IRPA) support, the process runs in parallel with Regulation 18 and provides a clear, consistent framework for addressing public criticism of match officials, particularly comments that may undermine the integrity of individuals or the sport, or fuel online abuse.

Rugby.title: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures
Rugby.summary: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures Ruck.co.uk
bullets: The 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia will expand from 20 to 24 nations, the first time that number has competed since 1999, with six pools of four. The top two in each pool and the four best third-placed teams will reach a new round of 16, so 16 nations advance. Teams play three pool matches instead of four, and champions will still play seven matches, with at least five rest days between games.

The tournament runs from 1 October to 13 November 2027 across seven Australian cities, opening with Australia against Hong Kong China in Perth. England and Wales meet in Pool F, Ireland are drawn with Scotland and Australia face New Zealand. Defending champions South Africa play Italy, Georgia and Romania, while England open against Tonga. The pool stage ends on 17 October, with the knockout stages beginning on 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
The 2027 Rugby World Cup will look very different, with the biggest overhaul of the tournament in more than two decades set to transform rugby's showpiece event. For the first time since 1999, the competition will feature 24 nations, with Australia preparing to host the biggest Rugby World Cup in history.

But the expansion is only half the story. World Rugby has introduced a completely new knockout stage, changed the pool structure and opened the door for teams finishing third to reach the last 16.

Racket.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m & delays doubles cuts decision
Racket.summary: The men's ATP Tour promises players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but delays a decision on hotly-disputed changes to doubles until next month.
Racket.copy:
The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month. The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event.

The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play. A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000.

Sonay Kartal believes the vitriolic abuse and threats that she and her fellow players receive after every match have become an unavoidable part of her job. “Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” the British No 2 says. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.

“You can try and take yourself away from it as much as you can and you can do different things to your [social media] account to try and hide it, but it’s a shame that it is something we have to deal with and hopefully it can change. Carlos Alcaraz continued his sensational late-season form as he outclassed world number five Daniil Medvedev to all but confirm his progress at the ATP Finals. But the 23-year-old Spaniard later said he had felt "a little problem" with his hamstring.

Alcaraz produced another sparkling display to control the contest throughout, despite ending the match with heavy strapping on his upper-left leg. Alcaraz received treatment and finished with heavy strapping on his upper-left leg. He said he felt "a little problem" with his hamstring, and that the next two days with his team and physio would be important. He has won three titles since returning in August.

Racket.copy:

Across five matches, Andreeva dropped just 26 games to claim the title on her debut singles appearance at the event. The opening set of her 7-5, 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday’s final was the only time she dropped more than four games in a set, beating the Ukrainian twice in Indian Wells alongside further round-robin victories against Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider, and a semi-final win versus Jessica Pegula.

Racket.title: Rising star Fils earns first ATP Finals win
Racket.summary: Rising star Arthur Fils claims his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.
Racket.copy:
Rising star Arthur Fils claimed his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin. Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.

Racket.title: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton to reach semi-finals
Racket.summary: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton to reach semi-finals BBC
bullets: World number one Alexander Zverev beat fourth-ranked Ben Shelton 6-2 7-6 (7-4) at the ATP Finals in Turin to reach the semi-finals with a match to spare. He lost two of 31 service points in the second set and extended his unbeaten run against Shelton to seven matches.

Zverev's win confirmed Rafael Jodar's elimination after Arthur Fils beat the Spaniard 4-6 6-2 6-2. Fils, the first Frenchman to win an ATP Finals match since 2011, plays Zverev on Thursday for a semi-final place. Britain's Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara lost their second doubles match.
Racket.copy:
World number one Alexander Zverev produced another serving masterclass against Ben Shelton to qualify for the ATP Finals knockout stage with a match to spare. The German, 29, lost just two of the 31 points played on his serve in the second set as he completed an impressive 6-2 7-6 (7-4) win over fourth-ranked Shelton.

The two-time champion only made 10 unforced errors and landed 25 winners in a ruthless display to reach the semi-finals at the season-ending tournament for a fifth time. The result confirmed Rafael Jodar's elimination, following the Spaniard's earlier 4-6 6-2 6-2 loss to French rising star Arthur Fils in the John McEnroe Group.

Racket.copy:

Wimbledon champions Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara received their trophy from the ATP's chief tour officer Andre Silva in Turin, after ending the season as the top-ranked men's doubles pairing for the first time.

In his acceptance speech, Patten, 30, called out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for their decision not to attend. "What a journey it has been. Turin is such a special place for us, we played a challenger just across the road when we ranked 60 and 40 in the world a couple of years ago. I never would have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now," said Patten.

Racket.title: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set!
Racket.summary: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set! WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- We came to Indian Wells to see what Mirra Andreeva would do in her first FAGE WTA Finals. We’re leaving without ever seeing her play a third set. She won all five matches, took all 10 sets and finished the week with a 61-26 edge in games. And on Sunday, she beat the same player she’d opened against, this time with a trophy waiting for her at the end.

At 19, Andreeva’s 7-5, 6-3 win in 1 hour and 48 minutes against Elina Svitolina made her the youngest WTA Finals champion since Maria Sharapova in 2004. A straight-sets sweep on debut puts her in even rarer company. Chris Evert did it at the inaugural edition in 1972, and Serena Williams won three matches in straight sets in 2001 before taking the title by walkover.

bullets: Mirra Andreeva, 19, won the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Sunday, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 in the final. The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina.

Golf.copy:
South Korea's A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers. Kim, who held a three-shot overnight lead, carded a third round 69 which included six birdies and three bogeys, with two of those coming on the final three holes, to reach 18 under overall.

"I really focused on my game. Just aim and hit, that's all," said Kim. "Today the wind direction [was a] little tricky, changed a lot, swirly in the air. That's golf." In the chase for the $4m (£3.1m) top prize at the season-ending event, Japan's Yuri Yoshida and Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand are both on 17 under - one shot behind Kim.

The 2026 PGA Tour season will last one day longer than expected. With pouring rain pummeling St. Simons Island, Georgia, the third round of the season-ending RSM Classic was postponed until Sunday. The final round will be played on Monday. It will be the PGA Tour’s third Monday finish of the fall slate.

“Obviously this is seaside golf, the golf course is very flat, the fairways are generally very flat with just a little bit of subtle movement,” PGA Tour chief referee Steve Rintoul told reporters on Saturday about the decision not to play on Saturday. “They’re above the marsh; they’re not sand-based. Even though it’s sea level, a dunes links look here, it’s not sand-based. So we had a lot of water sitting on the surface, especially in pockets in low areas in fairways where, I mentioned earlier, [we] may have a player who’s in the fairway in temporary water and needs to take relief, and that nearest point of relief takes him outside of the fairway. That takes the preferred lies out of his hands, and it just becomes, it’s not equitable when we get to that. So that kind of forced our hand.”

NAPLES, Fla. — Haeran Ryu of the Republic of Korea carded a bogey-free 6-under 66 on Thursday to sit T4 after the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship, one shot behind co-leaders Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson at Tiburón Golf Club.

Golf.title: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead
Golf.summary: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour's season finale has a crowded leaderboard after the first day. Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson each opened the CME Group Tour Championship at Tiburón Golf Club with a 7-under-par 65. They share the lead at -7, one stroke ahead of a nine-player group at -6. With three rounds still to play, very little separates the top of the 60-player field.

Thitikul is the most closely watched of the three co-leaders. The world No. 2 won this event in 2024 and 2025 and arrived in Naples trying to win the Tour Championship for a third year in a row. Her bogey-free-looking start of seven under puts her right in contention, although that bid is still three rounds away from being decided. A Lim Kim of South Korea and Karis Davidson of Australia matched her score, so the opening round produced a three-nation tie between Thailand, Korea and Australia.

Golf.summary: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play Yahoo
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It's one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions.

Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That's an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000.

Golf.title: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s
Golf.summary: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
A Lim Kim has the lead at the CME Group Tour Championship. But the player behind her is the one who has owned Tiburón Golf Club for the past two years. Jeeno Thitikul has won this event in each of the last two years. On Friday in Naples, Florida, she shot 67 in the second round. That made it nine rounds in a row in the 60s for her at this course, and it keeps her in the race for a third straight title.

Thitikul is alone in second place at 12-under 132, three shots behind A Lim Kim. Kim leads at 15-under 129. Two rounds remain in the LPGA Tour's season finale, so the final weekend of the year now has a clear chase story.

Golf.title: DP World Tour 2027: Fewer cards, LIV ban and returning stars
Golf.summary: DP World Tour 2027: Fewer cards, LIV ban and returning stars www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour has set its membership categories for the 2027 season, and the changes are significant. A total of 199 exempt members from 29 countries make up Categories 1 to 18. The number of full exempt cards falls from 110 to 100. Only the top 100 on the 2026 Race to Dubai Rankings keep full playing privileges, and players ranked 101 to 110 move into the conditional Category 18.

The pathways onto the tour are also narrower. At the Qualifying School Final Stage, the top 15 and ties now earn Category 18 membership, down from the top 20 and ties. Graduates from the HotelPlanner Tour, the tour's feeder circuit, fall from 20 to 15. Taken together, the changes are expected to leave about 20 fewer card holders in 2027.

Golf.summary: A BBC Sport investigation has found bills to UK companies were already overdue when LIV Golf made its final payments to players and executives before filing for bankruptcy.
bullets: BBC Sport has seen overdue invoices from five UK small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, unpaid by LIV Golf before it filed for bankruptcy. They include £321,671 owed to caterer Global Infusion Group and £75,225 owed to cleaning firm BD365 Clean.

Court filings show LIV paid golfers $16.6m on 31 July and $34.2m between 17 August and 3 September, including $6.4m to Jon Rahm. Only $2m has been earmarked for unsecured creditors, while LIV estimates liabilities of $500m to $1bn and at least 1,000 creditors.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf - backed by more than $5bn (£3.8bn) from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund - paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while leaving a trail of unpaid bills from UK suppliers.

BBC Sport has seen invoices from five small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, all of which were overdue before LIV made its final payments to players. Golf.title: DP World Tour Offers Star Invites To LIV Defectors
Golf.summary: DP World Tour Offers Star Invites To LIV Defectors Yahoo Sports
Golf.copy:
The professional golf world faces a new reality as the DP World Tour moves to fill its fields with high-profile names from the collapsing LIV Golf circuit. Nine players who left their original tours to join the Saudi-backed league have been offered a path back through sponsor invitations, a move that prioritizes star power over traditional meritocratic rankings. This shift comes as LIV Golf winds down through bankruptcy proceedings, leaving many players in limbo while tour officials scramble to stabilize the game's ecosystem.

According to Rediff, European Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings acknowledged the rapid shift in the sport, stating, "There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months." The tour is now offering these invitations without the hefty appearance fees that characterized the LIV era, aiming to inject excitement into lower-ranked events. This strategy targets specific stops that need a boost in star power, ensuring fields remain competitive even if depleted of top-tier members. According to Ronan MacNamara from Irish Golfer Magazine, up to 34 individuals previously associated with LIV are set to retain DP World Tour status in the coming year, a figure appearing inflated due to the former league's hostile maneuvers against the tour.

The most powerful word Brian Rolapp, the CEO of the PGA Tour, used late Monday afternoon while talking to reporters in a remote press conference was simple. Well, two longer forms of it, more precisely: simplify and simplification. The occasion was the announcement of the concluding work, conducted over the past 18 months, by the Tour’s Future Competition Committee, chaired by Tiger Woods, who was not present for this confab powered by . . . Microsoft Teams, the preferred video conferencing service of the PGA Tour.

Golf.summary: Columbia University Publishes Economic Impact Study of the 2025 Ryder Cup Ryder Cup | Official Site
Golf.copy:
Graduate students in Columbia University's Master of Science in Sports Management program have completed an independent economic impact study of the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black, delivering their findings to 2025 Ryder Cup executive staff. The project was conducted as a supervised research course led by Brian Connolly, founder and managing principal of Victus Advisors, during the fall 2025 semester.

“The Ryder Cup’s influence extends far beyond the golf course. As golf’s premier team event, it brings thousands of attendees from around the world and generates meaningful economic impact for local communities, businesses and the broader region. Having Columbia University independently assess that impact provided tremendous value to the PGA of America. We were particularly impressed by the rigor of the students’ work and appreciated the opportunity to give the next generation of sports industry leaders a firsthand look at what it takes to plan and deliver a global sporting event. Their work also provided valuable insight into the Ryder Cup’s impact on the host community." - David Charles, Senior Director of Championships, PGA of America

Golf.summary: DP World Tour Play-Offs: Race to Dubai battle and PGA Tour dual member cards decided in compelling climax DP World Tour
Golf.copy:
In a gripping climax to the DP World Tour season, the destiny of the 2026 Race to Dubai title went down to the final hole. For a time during Sunday's final round at the DP World Tour Championship, just one-tenth of a point separated Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy as the pair battled for the Race to Dubai crown.

With Tyrrell Hatton playing his way to a commanding victory, all eyes were on who would claim the Harry Vardon Trophy as the Tour's best-performing player across the 42-event campaign.

Golf.title: After historic Sunday, Rory McIlroy bullish about more than just his own game
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's Race to Dubai battle ended with a record-tying win and a glimpse of a bright future on the horizon. The post After historic Sunday, Rory McIlroy bullish about more than just his own game appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Sunday in Dubai ended with Rory McIlroy winning an emotional, history-tying eighth Race to Dubai title after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship, five shots behind winner Tyrrell Hatton. The second-place finish saw McIlroy narrowly pass Eugenio Chacarra, the 26-year-old Spaniard who finished tied for fourth, two shots behind McIlroy, for the season-long crown.

The victory left McIlroy emotional. After the win, McIlroy revealed that his father, Gerry, recently underwent a double lung transplant and that he spent nine days in the ICU. Rory said his father is doing well and told him to “go win the Race to Dubai,” which spurred McIlroy to chase down Chacarra and claim his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title. The win further cemented McIlroy’s status as one of, if not the, greatest European golfers in history.

Golf.title: Don't fall for this common golf setup myth, says top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Doug Spencer explains why you shouldn't try to use the same setup position for every shot. The post Don’t fall for this common golf setup myth, says top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Ask ten golfers on the range what they’re thinking about at address and you’ll likely get ten different answers: Keep your head down. Bend 45 degrees at the hips. Square your feet. Keep your left arm rigid.

We’ve been conditioned to view the golf setup as a static checklist of rules — a rigid pose designed simply to hold us in place before the action begins. That mindset is one of the biggest reasons golfers struggle with consistency.

Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau has a new job — golf course designer. Here’s his first project Golfweek
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has announced The Orchard, a 450-acre master-planned golf community with an 18-hole championship course, in his hometown of Clovis, California. It is the first project of his new course design firm, DeChambeau Designs, in partnership with Clovis-based developer Cook Land Company. The site is the historic McFarlane Ranch. Plans include homes, a clubhouse, a public farmers market and programmes giving local youth and schools access to the sport.

The announcement comes as LIV Golf has shut down and players are seeking 2027 playing rights. DeChambeau's 2024 US Open win makes him eligible for full DP World Tour membership, but he has not confirmed whether he applied before the mid-November deadline. He is scheduled to play December's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa. Rory McIlroy said DeChambeau draws eyeballs to tournaments but does not appear to have many options.

bullets: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has defended the decision to welcome back former LIV Golf players, calling it a "huge opportunity". LIV confirmed two weeks ago that it will wind down operations four years after launching and spending more than $5bn. Several LIV players have struck deals for 2027, and Joaquin Niemann and Lucas Herbert have reportedly agreed to play at least 15 events each through wild cards. Some existing members believe access should be earned on merit.

Kinnings said stronger fields would arrive at a time of year when dual members are in the United States, benefiting promoters, sponsors and broadcasters. Bryson DeChambeau is eligible for 2027 as a recent major champion, and a membership announcement is expected on Tuesday. Kinnings said the tour is in "very positive" talks with the PGA Tour, which from 2028 will run a two-tier structure with top-tier purses of at least $20m, and hopes for news by the New Year.
Golf.copy:

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s most successful player signs major DP World Tour deal
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s most successful player signs major DP World Tour deal Today's Golfer
bullets: Joaquin Niemann, who won nine individual events and earned $88m in prize money across five LIV Golf seasons, has signed a DP World Tour deal giving him between 15 and 20 tournament invites next season, according to Golf Channel Latin America. The invites are likely to fall between February and August and will not include the Rolex Series events.

The 28-year-old has no tour status but can play the circuit because it has offered packages of guaranteed invites to non-members returning from LIV. He remains banned on the PGA Tour until at least next August. Lucas Herbert is also set to sign a similar deal. The tour will confirm on 17 November whether Bryson DeChambeau, eligible through his 2024 US Open win, has taken a card for 2027.
Golf.copy:
A number of LIV Golf stars are converging on the DP World Tour, including the breakaway league’s most successful player. He earned $88million in prize money across his five seasons yet still did not top the inordinate earnings table at LIV Golf. But there can be no doubt that, with his nine individual victories, Joaquin Niemann was the most successful player on the now-doomed breakaway league.

What the Chilean’s dominance during this period will mean for his legacy can and will be disputed, but Niemann is returning to golf’s traditional tours as a winner on LIV, the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour.

Golf.title: First win for Duncan after 12 years & 222 attempts
Golf.summary: American Lindy Duncan wins The Annika for her first LPGA Tour title after playing in 222 events over 12 years.
bullets: American Lindy Duncan, 35, won her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd attempt at The Annika, finishing 16 under after a final-round 67 at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida. She began the day one shot ahead and was tied with South Korea's Choi Hye-jin with two holes left, before two late birdies secured a two-shot victory. Duncan joined the tour in 2014 and had only one top-10 finish this season.

The win lifted Duncan from 74th to 34th in the season-long points race, qualifying her for the 60-player CME Group Tour Championship. World number one Nelly Korda finished seventh and will aim to win a second title of the season at the finale next week. England's Lottie Woad, also in the field for the finale, secured a top-10 finish. Duncan said she was "completely shocked" and thanked those who believed in her.
Golf.copy:
American Lindy Duncan was left "completely shocked" after winning her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd time of asking. The 35-year-old started Sunday's final round of The Annika with a one-shot lead and two late birdies saw her claim victory.

Duncan, who joined the tour in 2014, had only enjoyed one top-10 finish this season. But her three-under-par 67 saw her finish on 16 under at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida, two shots clear of her nearest challenger, South Korea's Choi Hye-jin .

Golf.title: 'I'm back': Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards
Golf.summary: Ten players earned PGA Tour cards via the DP World Tour on Sunday, including Patrick Reed, ex-LIV pros and a former delivery driver. The post ‘I’m back’: Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Patrick Reed has secured a PGA Tour card for 2027 via the DP World Tour's season-long points race, which offers 10 cards. He finished second among players without full PGA Tour status, behind Eugenio Chacarra, who took the top spot and will also be in early Signature Events and the Players Championship. Reed left LIV earlier this year. He won in Dubai and Qatar and finished T2 in Bahrain, plus a T12 at the Masters and T10 at the PGA Championship.

The future of the 10-card pathway is uncertain, with the DP World Tour-PGA Tour alliance up in the air. Competition is expected to increase in 2027 with an influx of former LIV players. Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship on Sunday and finished third in the Race to Dubai, but was ineligible for a card because of his LIV season. Reed said the decision to leave LIV came with only one year to qualify, and that returning would let him play closer to home.
Golf.copy:
On Sunday in Dubai, Patrick Reed made it official. “I’m back,” he said as he accepted a metal PGA Tour card and flashed a wide grin. “It feels good.” Reed left LIV earlier this year and, facing a one-year ban from the PGA Tour, turned his attention to the DP World Tour, where he hoped to earn one of 10 PGA Tour cards available via the season-long points race.

He took the drama out of that quest in just a few tournaments, winning in Dubai, finishing T2 in Bahrain and winning in Qatar in three consecutive early season events. Add in a T12 at the Masters and a T10 at the PGA Championship and he’d wrapped up his return pre-summertime.
